emergency.notes: Qatar uses a single universal emergency number (999) for all services. English-speaking operators available. Qatar Tourism Police: +974-4800-7777.

embassies.name: U.S. Embassy Doha
embassies.address: 22 February Street, Al Luqta District, Doha

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Qatar. Qatar is one of the safest countries in the world for tourists. Violent crime is extremely rare. Be aware of strict laws regarding alcohol, drugs, and public behavior.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Qatar is generally a safe destination. Most visits are trouble-free. Be aware of local laws, particularly regarding alcohol consumption, dress code, and same-sex relationships.

healthcare.systemType: Excellent public/private system. Hamad Medical Corporation runs the main public hospitals. Quality private hospitals also available.
healthcare.costForTourists: Healthcare is very high quality. Emergency care at public hospitals covered for life-threatening emergencies. Private clinic visit $100-250. Hospital admission $500-2,500/night. Travel insurance strongly recommended.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies widely available, many open 24 hours. English-speaking pharmacists common. Most common medications available.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Hamad General Hospital is the main public hospital. Sidra Medicine and Aspetar are world-class specialized hospitals. English is widely spoken at all medical facilities.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance recommended. Healthcare costs are significant. Hamad Medical Corporation provides emergency care regardless of insurance.

controlledSubstances.note: Require prior approval from Qatar Ministry of Public Health. Carry original prescription and doctor's letter. Maximum 3-month supply.
Strictly illegal. Zero tolerance. Possession can result in imprisonment and deportation.
Require documentation from prescribing physician. Carry in original packaging.
Many common cold medications containing pseudoephedrine may be restricted. Check current list with Qatar Ministry of Public Health.

medications.generalAdvice: Qatar has strict drug laws. Carry all medications in original packaging with prescriptions. Apply for prior approval for controlled substances at qatar.gov.qa before travel.

scams.name: Unofficial taxi overcharging
scams.description: Unmetered unofficial taxis offer rides at flat rates that far exceed metered fares, especially at Hamad International Airport.
scams.avoidance: Use Karwa (official metered taxis) or Uber/Careem app for transparent pricing. Official taxis are orange and white.

scams.name: Souvenir quality misrepresentation
scams.description: Vendors claim handicrafts, carpets, and goods are local Qatari-made when they are mass-produced imports from China or India.
scams.avoidance: Accept that most souvenirs are imported. Buy for sentimental value not authenticity claims. Government-certified Qatari craft shops exist in the souq.

scams.name: Ticket scalping for major events
scams.description: For major football matches and events, third-party sellers charge multiples of face value for tickets that may be counterfeit.
scams.avoidance: Purchase event tickets through official channels only (Qatar Tourism app, official event websites).

scams.name: Phishing via QR codes at restaurants
scams.description: Fake QR codes placed over legitimate menu QR codes redirect to phishing sites collecting payment details or personal information.
scams.avoidance: Verify the URL when scanning QR codes matches the restaurant's official domain. Use contactless payment or cash when uncertain.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIMs from Ooredoo or Vodafone Qatar at Hamad International Airport. $15-30 for packages with 10-50GB. eSIM available via Airalo. Excellent 5G coverage nationwide.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent free WiFi in malls, hotels, and most restaurants. Hamad International Airport has free WiFi. Public WiFi in Lusail City and Doha waterfront.
connectivity.bestOption: Ooredoo tourist SIM for best coverage. eSIM for convenience.

cultural.tipping: Not culturally required but appreciated. Restaurants: 10-15% if not included. Hotel staff: QAR 10-20 per service. Taxis: round up to nearest riyal.
cultural.dressCode: Dress modestly in public — shoulders and knees covered for both men and women. In malls, mosques, and government buildings, dress code is enforced. Swimwear only at private beaches and hotel pools. Bikinis acceptable at resort beaches.
cultural.greetings: Standard greeting is 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you). Men may greet men with handshake and nose-to-nose touch. Women and men do not typically shake hands unless woman initiates. Use right hand for greetings and food.
taboos: Public displays of affection (kissing or cuddling in public can result in fines or arrest)
Drinking alcohol outside licensed venues (hotels, licensed restaurants)
Loud or disruptive behavior in public
Disrespecting Islam, Qatar's ruling family, or government
Photographing people without consent, especially women
Photographing government buildings, palaces, or military facilities
cultural.haggling: Acceptable at Souq Waqif for crafts and clothing. Not practiced in malls, chain restaurants, or supermarkets.

safety.lgbtSafety: Same-sex relationships are illegal under Qatari law and can result in imprisonment and deportation. All LGBTQ+ activity should be conducted with absolute discretion. Qatar has a zero tolerance policy.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Qatar is very safe for solo female travelers by regional standards. Harassment is rare. Modest dress required in public. Women can drive, travel alone, and access all public areas without restriction.
safety.notes: Qatar is one of the safest countries in the world for tourists. Violent crime is almost nonexistent. The main risks for tourists are strict local laws regarding alcohol, drugs, dress code, and personal behavior that differs from Western norms. Extreme heat in summer is a serious concern.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US, UK, EU, Australia, and many others receive visa-free or visa on arrival access for 30-180 days. Check qatar.gov.qa for current visa policy.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: November-April (pleasant 18-30°C). Avoid May-September (extreme heat 38-50°C). National Day on December 18 features spectacular celebrations.

hospitals.name: Hamad General Hospital
hospitals.address: Al Rayyan Road, West Bay, Doha
hospitals.notes: Qatar's main public hospital and trauma center. World-class facilities. English spoken by most staff.

hospitals.name: Sidra Medicine
hospitals.address: Al Luqta Street, Education City, Doha
hospitals.notes: World-class hospital affiliated with Weill Cornell Medicine. Excellent international-standard care.

hospitals.name: Aspetar Orthopaedic and Sports Medicine Hospital
hospitals.notes: Internationally ranked sports medicine and orthopaedic hospital. Best for sports injuries.

immediate: Stay indoors between 10am and 4pm during summer months (June-September)
Drink at least 3-4 liters of water per day
Wear lightweight, loose, light-colored clothing outdoors
Never leave children or pets in parked vehicles
Seek air-conditioned spaces immediately if experiencing dizziness or nausea
after: Seek medical attention for signs of heat stroke: hot dry skin, confusion, loss of consciousness
Check on vulnerable companions after extreme heat events

immediate: Stay indoors with windows and doors closed
Turn off air conditioning to prevent dust infiltration
If driving, reduce speed to a crawl and turn on hazard lights, or pull over safely
Cover nose and mouth with damp cloth if caught outdoors
Stay away from the sea during dust storms
after: Check air quality index before going outdoors
Clean vehicle air filters after major sandstorms
Replace indoor air filters after significant dust infiltration
